newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on covering, weak Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on covering, weak Tokyo.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed after positive sentiment from short-covering bids were offset by a weak late session in Tokyo futures, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 313 cents ($1.25) a kg, up half cent from Wednesday. November SMR 20 buyer fell a cent to 307.50 cents.
Traders quoted the SMR20 at around 303, SMR CV at 365, SMR L at 346, SMR5 at 315, SMR10 at 304 and drum latex at 235.
"The market has gone quiet again," said a dealer. "There was hardly any trading today."
Another trader said she noted only short-covering by local agents for earlier sales made to Europe. "It looks like it'll be a free fall (for prices) from now unless demand returns."
Traders said producers were also becoming reserved of selling at low levels due to rains which returned this week.
"The last three weeks were dry and a lot of rubber had come into the market, making sentiment bearish," a trader said.
The INRO five-day average was 241.88 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 1 from 242.47 on Oct 2. The daily indicator was 241.24 against 241.58.
